These functions visualize the space--time errors computed by the three
convergence notebooks. Each column of `errors` corresponds to one value of
`alpha_vector`, and each row to an entry of `x_axis_vector`. The plotted
quantity is

\[
E=\|u-U_{h,m}^{\tau}\|_{L_2(0,T;L_2(\Gamma))}.
\]

The error analysis motivates, for \(0<\alpha<2\), a bound of the form

\[
E\lesssim \tau+h^{\min\{\alpha+2s,2\}-\epsilon}
+h^{\alpha-2}e^{-c_\alpha\sqrt m},\qquad
c_\alpha=2\pi\sqrt{1-\alpha/2},
\]

under the required data regularity, rational approximation accuracy, and
spectral coverage assumptions. Here \(s\in[0,1]\) describes data
regularity and \(\epsilon>0\) is sufficiently small. Finite sums of
eigenfunctions are smooth, so the spatial prediction saturates at
\(2-\epsilon\). The notebooks use reference slopes 2 in \(h\), 1 in
\(\tau\), and \(-c_\alpha\) on the \(\sqrt m\) scale. The computed
finite-mode rational experiment uses the last exponent as a bound benchmark;
it does not establish uniform spectral accuracy or require an observed
finite-order slope equal to \(-c_\alpha\).

The notebooks fit the observed rates before calling these plotters:

\[
\log E=s_h\log h+b_h,\qquad
\log E=s_\tau\log\tau+b_\tau,\qquad
\ln E=s_m\sqrt m+b_m.
\]

Changing the logarithm base on both axes leaves the first two slopes
unchanged. The rational slope uses the natural logarithm specifically.
The plotters display supplied slopes and guide curves; they do not estimate
rates or compute the numerical errors. Positive errors and positive axis
values are needed for the logarithmic scales and line constructors below.

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(reshape2)
```

## `loglog_line_equation()`

Returns a function describing a power law with slope `slope` \(=p\)
through the positive point `(x1, y1)`:

\[
y(x)=Cx^p,\qquad C=\frac{y_1}{x_1^p},\qquad
\log_{10}y=p\log_{10}x+\log_{10}C.
\]

`b` is \(\log_{10}C\). The returned closure evaluates \(x^p10^b\)
on a vector of new positive `x` values. This supplies the straight guides
for the spatial and temporal plots on logarithmic axes.

```{r}
loglog_line_equation <- function(x1, y1, slope) {
  b <- log10(y1 / (x1 ^ slope))
  
  function(x) {
    (x ^ slope) * (10 ^ b)
  }
}
```

## `exp_line_equation()`

Returns an exponential curve of logarithmic slope `slope` \(=p\) through
the positive ordinate `(x1, y1)`:

\[
y(x)=Ce^{px},\qquad \ln C=\ln y_1-px_1.
\]

`lnC` stores this intercept, and the returned closure evaluates the curve at
new `x` values. For the rational study, the caller supplies the transformed
coordinate \(x=\sqrt m\) and \(p=-c_\alpha\), giving
\(y(m)=C e^{-c_\alpha\sqrt m}\). The transformation occurs in the
plotter, not in this constructor.

```{r}
exp_line_equation <- function(x1, y1, slope) {
  lnC <- log(y1) - slope * x1
  
  function(x) {
    exp(lnC + slope * x)
  }
}
```

## `compute_guiding_lines()`

Builds one reference curve per error column using the supplied slope, with
vertical placement determined by all data points. Let \(x_i\) denote the
coordinates already transformed by the caller, \(E_{ij}\) the error
matrix, and \(p_j\) `theoretical_rates[j]`. Through each observation
\((x_k,E_{kj})\), `line_equation_fun()` constructs a curve
\(\ell_{kj}\). The returned matrix is

\[
G_{ij}=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^n\ell_{kj}(x_i).
\]

For the power-law constructor this is

\[
G_{ij}=C_jx_i^{p_j},\qquad
C_j=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^n\frac{E_{kj}}{x_k^{p_j}},
\]

and for the exponential constructor it is

\[
G_{ij}=C_je^{p_jx_i},\qquad
C_j=\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^n E_{kj}e^{-p_jx_k}.
\]

`guiding_lines_aux[, k]` stores the curve anchored at observation `k`, and
`rowMeans()` averages ordinates in the original error units. Thus the
guide keeps the requested slope but its amplitude is an arithmetic average
of anchored amplitudes, rather than a fitted intercept or a rigorous
upper-bound constant. The result has `length(x_axis_vector)` rows and
`length(theoretical_rates)` columns. `errors` must have these same
dimensions, and the constructor must accept `x1`, `y1`, and `slope`.

```{r}
compute_guiding_lines <- function(x_axis_vector, errors, theoretical_rates, line_equation_fun) {
  guiding_lines <- matrix(NA, nrow = length(x_axis_vector), ncol = length(theoretical_rates))
  
  for (j in seq_along(theoretical_rates)) {
    guiding_lines_aux <- matrix(NA, nrow = length(x_axis_vector), ncol = length(x_axis_vector))
    
    for (k in seq_along(x_axis_vector)) {
      point_x1 <- x_axis_vector[k]
      point_y1 <- errors[k, j]
      slope <- theoretical_rates[j]
      
      line <- line_equation_fun(x1 = point_x1, y1 = point_y1, slope = slope)
      guiding_lines_aux[, k] <- line(x_axis_vector)
    }
    
    guiding_lines[, j] <- rowMeans(guiding_lines_aux)
  }
  
  return(guiding_lines)
}
```

## `error.convergence.plotter()`

Returns a `ggplot` object containing observed error points joined by solid
curves and the matching reference guides drawn with dashed curves. Inputs
`theoretical_rates` and `observed_rates` have one entry per `alpha_vector`
value; titles and the horizontal label are supplied by the caller.

For `apply_sqrt = FALSE`, the plot uses base-10 logarithmic axes, the
coordinates are the supplied \(h\) or \(\tau\), and the caller uses
`loglog_line_equation`. For `apply_sqrt = TRUE`, `x_vec` is
\(\sqrt{\texttt{x_axis_vector}}\), the vertical axis is natural-logarithmic,
and the caller uses `exp_line_equation`. Rational-order ticks are positioned
at \(\sqrt m\) but labelled with the original \(m\) values.

`compute_guiding_lines()` receives these plotted coordinates. `melt()`
converts the error matrix to one row per observation and alpha for `ggplot`.
Matching colors associate observed curves with their guides. The legend
shows alpha, reference slope (called a bound benchmark in square-root mode),
and the supplied observed slope. `theme_minimal()` and the Palatino font
set presentation only; the function neither saves files nor changes errors.

```{r}
error.convergence.plotter <- function(x_axis_vector, 
                                      alpha_vector, 
                                      errors, 
                                      theoretical_rates, 
                                      observed_rates,
                                      line_equation_fun,
                                      fig_title,
                                      x_axis_label,
                                      apply_sqrt = FALSE) {
  
  x_vec <- if (apply_sqrt) sqrt(x_axis_vector) else x_axis_vector
  
  guiding_lines <- compute_guiding_lines(x_axis_vector = x_vec, 
                                         errors = errors, 
                                         theoretical_rates = theoretical_rates, 
                                         line_equation_fun = line_equation_fun)
  
  default_colors <- scales::hue_pal()(length(alpha_vector))
  
  plot_lines <- lapply(1:ncol(guiding_lines), function(i) {
    geom_line(
      data = data.frame(x = x_vec, y = guiding_lines[, i]),
      aes(x = x, y = y),
      color = default_colors[i],
      linetype = "dashed",
      show.legend = FALSE
    )
  })
  
  df <- as.data.frame(cbind(x_vec, errors))
  colnames(df) <- c("x_axis_vector", alpha_vector)
  df_melted <- melt(df, id.vars = "x_axis_vector", variable.name = "column", value.name = "value")
  
  custom_labels <- paste0(formatC(alpha_vector, format = "f", digits = 2), 
                          " | ", 
                          formatC(theoretical_rates, format = "f", digits = 4), 
                          " | ", 
                          formatC(observed_rates, format = "f", digits = 4))
  
  df_melted$column <- factor(df_melted$column, levels = alpha_vector, labels = custom_labels)

  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_line(data = df_melted, aes(x = x_axis_vector, y = value, color = column)) +
    geom_point(data = df_melted, aes(x = x_axis_vector, y = value, color = column)) +
    plot_lines +
    labs(
      title = fig_title,
      x = x_axis_label,
      y = expression(Error),
      color = if (apply_sqrt) "alpha | bound benchmark | observed" else "alpha | theoretical | observed"
    ) +
    (if (apply_sqrt) {
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = x_vec, labels = round(x_axis_vector, 4))
    } else {
      scale_x_log10(breaks = x_axis_vector, labels = round(x_axis_vector, 4))
    }) +
    (if (apply_sqrt) {
      scale_y_continuous(trans = "log", labels = scales::scientific_format())
    } else {
      scale_y_log10(labels = scales::scientific_format())
    }) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(text = element_text(family = "Palatino"),
          legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.direction = "vertical",
          plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 18, face = "bold"))
  
  return(p)
}
```

## `errorConvergencePlotterLatex()`

Returns the publication-style `ggplot` with the same observations, guiding
lines, and coordinate choices as `error.convergence.plotter()`. The caller
also supplies `y_axis_label` and `color_label`; labels may contain LaTeX
for later TikZ export by `myggsave()`.

For spatial and temporal studies (`apply_sqrt = FALSE`), the legend adds
the relative percentage difference between each nonzero reference slope
\(p_j\) and supplied fitted slope \(\widehat p_j\):

\[
100\frac{|p_j-\widehat p_j|}{|p_j|}.
\]

This is `relative_per_error`, a comparison of slopes rather than a relative
solution error. For the rational study (`apply_sqrt = TRUE`), the legend
contains only alpha, the bound exponent benchmark, and the fitted slope.
Although the percentage vector is computed at entry, that branch does not
display it: an upper-bound benchmark does not prescribe equality of slopes.

The nested `scientific_ticks()` helper formats the logarithmic-axis breaks
in scientific notation and removes redundant zeros and plus signs from the
exponent. Square-root mode instead labels breaks by integer \(m\), keeping
their positions at \(\sqrt m\), and explicitly uses a base-\(e\)
logarithmic vertical transformation. The remaining differences are larger
points, lines, and text. The return is an unsaved plot object.

```{r}
errorConvergencePlotterLatex <- function(x_axis_vector, 
                                      alpha_vector, 
                                      errors, 
                                      theoretical_rates, 
                                      observed_rates,
                                      line_equation_fun,
                                      fig_title,
                                      x_axis_label,
                                      y_axis_label,
                                      color_label,
                                      apply_sqrt = FALSE) {

  relative_per_error <- 100 * abs(theoretical_rates - observed_rates) / abs(theoretical_rates)
  
  x_vec <- if (apply_sqrt) sqrt(x_axis_vector) else x_axis_vector
  
  guiding_lines <- compute_guiding_lines(x_axis_vector = x_vec, 
                                         errors = errors, 
                                         theoretical_rates = theoretical_rates, 
                                         line_equation_fun = line_equation_fun)
  
  default_colors <- scales::hue_pal()(length(alpha_vector))
  
  plot_lines <- lapply(1:ncol(guiding_lines), function(i) {
    geom_line(
      data = data.frame(x = x_vec, y = guiding_lines[, i]),
      aes(x = x, y = y),
      color = default_colors[i],
      linetype = "dashed",
      linewidth = 0.6,
      show.legend = FALSE
    )
  })
  
  df <- as.data.frame(cbind(x_vec, errors))
  colnames(df) <- c("x_axis_vector", alpha_vector)
  df_melted <- melt(df, id.vars = "x_axis_vector", variable.name = "column", value.name = "value")
  if (apply_sqrt) {
    custom_labels <- sprintf("$%s \\; | \\; %s \\; | \\; %s$",
      formatC(alpha_vector, format = "f", digits = 2),
      formatC(theoretical_rates, format = "f", digits = 4),
      formatC(observed_rates, format = "f", digits = 4))
  } else {
    custom_labels <- sprintf("$%s \\; | \\; %s \\; | \\; %s \\; | \\; %s$",
      formatC(alpha_vector, format = "f", digits = 2),
      formatC(theoretical_rates, format = "f", digits = 4),
      formatC(observed_rates, format = "f", digits = 4),
      formatC(relative_per_error, format = "f", digits = 2))
  }

  df_melted$column <- factor(df_melted$column, levels = alpha_vector, labels = custom_labels)

  scientific_ticks <- function(x) {
    labels <- formatC(x, format = "e", digits = 2)
    labels <- sub("0+e", "e", labels)
    labels <- sub("[.]e", "e", labels)
    labels <- sub("e([+-])0+([0-9]+)$", "e\\1\\2", labels)
    sub("e[+]", "e", labels)
  }

  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_line(data = df_melted, aes(x = x_axis_vector, y = value, color = column), linewidth = 1.6) +
    geom_point(data = df_melted, aes(x = x_axis_vector, y = value, color = column), size = 2) +
    plot_lines +
    labs(
      title = fig_title,
      x = x_axis_label,
      y = y_axis_label,
      color = color_label
    ) +
    (if (apply_sqrt) {
      scale_x_continuous(breaks = x_vec, labels = formatC(x_axis_vector, format = "f", digits = 0))
    } else {
      scale_x_log10(breaks = x_axis_vector, labels = scientific_ticks)
    }) +
    (if (apply_sqrt) {
      #scale_y_continuous(trans = "log", labels = scales::scientific_format())
      scale_y_continuous(trans = scales::log_trans(base = exp(1)), labels = scales::scientific_format())
    } else {
      scale_y_log10(labels = scales::scientific_format())
    }) +
    theme_minimal() +
    # theme(text = element_text(family = "Palatino"),
    #       legend.position = "bottom",
    #       legend.direction = "vertical",
    #       #plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
    #       plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 18, face = "plain")) +
    theme(
  text = element_text(family = "Palatino", size = 18),

  plot.title = element_text(
    hjust = 0.5,
    size = 20,
    face = "plain"
  ),

  axis.title.x = element_text(size = 14),
  axis.title.y = element_text(size = 14),

  axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12),
  axis.text.y = element_text(size = 12),

  legend.title = element_text(size = 14),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 12),

  legend.position = "bottom",
  legend.direction = "vertical"
)
  
  return(p)
}
```
